multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which statement about a language model's output is accurate?

choice.div: It is generated text whose plausibility is not evidence of truth.
It is retrieved from a verified knowledge base.
It is reliable when the model says it is certain.

div.p: The model predicts text. Certainty is a style, not a confidence measurement.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A task is low-cost, reversible, and quick to check. Which tier applies?

choice.div: Use now, with a read before it leaves.
Use with review by a second team.

div.p: Low consequence and cheap verification are exactly the conditions for direct use.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: What is the correct first step when a request needs data you may not paste?

choice.div: Stop and use the system that owns the data, or reduce it to placeholders.
Paste it and delete the chat afterwards.
Use a personal account to avoid the company's retention.

div.p: The decision is made before the paste. Owning systems carry the accountability the chat window does not.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which draft is ready to send?

choice.div: The one whose numbers were read from the source and whose policy claims name a document.
The one that reads most smoothly.
The one produced by the newest model.

div.p: Readiness is a property of the checks performed, not the prose or the model version.

choiceresponse.p: Which habits reduce the chance an AI error reaches a customer? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Naming the claims in a draft before sending it.
Recomputing any number that will be quoted.
Recording what was checked and by whom.
Labelling unverified statements or removing them.
Trusting the draft more when it is long and detailed.

div.p: Verification is a routine: name, source, compare, record. Length and detail are not controls.
